column.text: Bitcoin is currently trading at sixty-four thousand two hundred eighty-eight dollars with a one-day RSI of fifty-two point four, signaling neutral momentum that has ample room to run before hitting overbought territory. Despite the tape appearing range-bound and mixed without a clear directional tailwind, we are firmly in an accumulation phase where distribution pressure is being effectively limited by strong institutional demand flowing through ETFs. Yesterday alone, Bitcoin spot exchange traded funds posted a net inflow of one hundred eighty-nine point three million dollars while Ethereum counterparts registered seventy-one point four million, proving that new money entry rather than leveraged speculation drives this move. The dominant signal remains sustained buying pressure combined with rising open interest in Solana indicating genuine fresh capital participation. However, the macro backdrop is contracting as thirty-year US Treasury yields surged to five percent thirty-one percent alongside six hundred billion dollars added to national debt since July first. This dollar liquidity contraction forces risk assets into a headwind where demand for proof on continuation longs becomes paramount and failed rallies should be treated as better odds shorts rather than breakout traps. We must avoid the R-to-R two-to-four mid zone that historically bleeds capital during these transitions. While whale alerts show accumulation over twenty-nine billion dollars in Bitcoin over sixty days triggering short liquidations, regulatory headlines regarding SEC rules could still trigger panic selling before midterms if macro data fails to support continued rate cuts.
